sections.title: Executive Verdict
paragraphs: Prevest Denpro is a profitable dental-materials manufacturer with recurring consumables, international distribution and substantial cash. The strongest evidence is a multi-year organic incremental-capital return near 30%, supported by actual operating cash generation. The concerns are a contestable moat, uneven new-product execution, governance and disclosure lapses, and a price that asks more than the conservative operating case delivers.

At the dated secondary historical reference close of ₹405 on 19 October 2026, the base case earns 8.77% nominal pretax annually over 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, below the 15% equity hurdle. The conditional 15% entry estimate is ₹307.00, not an executable bid or recommendation. Full investment attractiveness remains NS because the complete 60-session liquidity and restrictions evidence is unavailable. This is a research/watchlist candidate, not a certified compounder or a distressed financing situation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
paragraphs: Prevest Denpro Limited: ISIN INE0GAO01018, CIN L85199JK1999PLC001969, BSE 543363. Research cutoff: 20 October 2026. Market reference: 19 October 2026. The dated interop master confirms 12,003,000 issued shares, a 200-share lot and SM series. A shareholder migration resolution is not evidence of completed main-board trading; the company remains in this SME research cohort. Financial statements follow Indian AS. Valuation uses consolidated FY26 plus the limited-reviewed June 2026 quarter to build a comparable TTM.

Confidence is high on the audited headline operating balances, medium on normalized organic capital economics and treasury accessibility, and low on complete execution capacity and current mutual-fund NAV. The disputed FY21 cash-flow subtotal is disclosed and excluded from the cumulative cash-scoring window. Regulatory claims are issuer disclosures, not independent verification of each live certificate. Modelled October cash is a dated bridge from March cash, not an observed October bank statement.

G1 is Conditional for disclosed remuneration and filing lapses, despite subsequent shareholder approval. G2 is Conditional for an apparently stale investment-NAV table, bounded by excluding all mutual funds from funding and value. G3 is Clear under conservative cash-linked funding tests. G4 is Conditional: lot and dated price are verified, but surveillance and a complete 60-session tape are not. No material Hold or Fail is imposed solely because private daily bank statements are unavailable.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
paragraphs: All 13 factors use the same score wherever referenced. Exact Decimal weights and contributions are retained. Displays use conventional ROUND_HALF_UP at one decimal. IAS uses unrounded BQS and never substitutes a neutral score for missing liquidity. Missing-factor bounds are diagnostic, not a point estimate.

The persistent weak-cash ceiling is explicitly tested. Reported five-year CFO/PAT of 0.719 warrants investigation, but does not mechanically imply CASH 3. Investing-classified deposit interest explains part of the gap; ₹33.85 crore remains after actual capex. CASH 6 and CAP 7 do not trigger the GQS ceiling. A separate sensitivity sets CASH to 3 and applies the GQS cap of 5. These methodology thresholds organize judgment; they are not empirically validated return predictors.

sections.title: Business Overview
paragraphs: The company develops and manufactures materials for restorative dentistry, endodontics, prosthodontics, preventive care and laboratory use. Products include cements, filling and bonding materials, root-canal products, impression materials and newer digital resins, disinfectants and Oradox oral-care products. Dentists and distributors buy relatively small-ticket consumables repeatedly as procedures occur. Product reliability, clinical familiarity, availability and distributor support matter more than a single equipment order.

FY26 consolidated net operating revenue is ₹71.8085 crore, not total income of ₹76.7236 crore. Gross geographic sales comprise exports of ₹42.2346 crore and domestic sales of ₹30.7647 crore. Exports are therefore 57.86% of gross product sales, not a verified 60% of net revenue. The bridge is gross sales of ₹72.9993 crore, less discounts of ₹2.1049 crore, plus other operating revenue of ₹0.8697 crore and freight of ₹0.0444 crore. Geographic totals and net revenue must not be mixed.

The main manufacturing site is in Samba, Jammu and Kashmir. The issuer reports installed output capacity above 200 MT and distribution to over 90 countries. Country count is not a measure of sales diversity by value; customer and distributor concentration remain ND. Denvisio Biomed, Axiodent US and Prevest Denpro Gulf are incorporated subsidiaries, not identified acquisitions. FY26 Axiodent sales were only ₹0.1263 crore and Gulf sales nil, so they do not yet warrant large independent valuation blocks.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
paragraphs: The plausible advantage combines formulation know-how, consistent manufacturing, regulatory dossiers, dentist education and distribution at competitive prices. Repeat purchases and high value added can support good margins with limited fixed assets. That can be a good business without being a monopoly. No measured retention rate, pricing-power series, patent barrier or switching-cost study was disclosed. Private-label US sales improve factory utilization but can leave the customer relationship and brand value with a distributor.

Issuer-reported ISO 13485, MDSAP, CE, CDSCO and product-specific USFDA/SFDA access support entry into regulated markets. They are not universal FDA approval of every product or exclusive rights. Individual current certificate status was not independently authenticated. Manufacturing-quality failures, adverse clinical outcomes, counterfeits or distribution disruption could harm a small brand disproportionately.

Competitive references include Solventum Dental Solutions, Shofu, Dentsply Sirona and GC. Solventum Dental Solutions reported 2025 sales of US$1,349 million, 3.3% organic growth and a 25.6% segment operating margin. Shofu FY25 sales of JPY38,698 million and operating profit of JPY5,392 million imply a 13.93% margin. Dentsply Essential Dental Solutions had FY24 sales of US$1,454 million and a 0.1% organic decline. GC is a broad private dental incumbent. These are dated competitive references, not a comparable current-multiple basket: product mix, geography, accounting and corporate costs differ.

High dental-consumables margins are economically plausible, but global rivals also have materials science, clinical evidence and digital-workflow products. Management claims of digital leadership earn no unsupported moat bonus. MOAT 6 reflects useful, profitable but contestable advantages.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
paragraphs: The preselected primary window is standalone FY21 to FY26. Operating revenue grew from ₹28.4760 crore to ₹71.6642 crore, a 20.27% CAGR. The more recent FY23 to FY26 window grew from ₹49.8541 crore, a 12.86% CAGR. Absolute annual increments are preserved alongside percentages. Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue increased 20.94%, from ₹15.7663 crore to ₹19.0683 crore. One quarter is insufficient for a trajectory bonus; REV starts at 8 with a net adjustment of zero.

Classification changes are not organic growth. FY22 original operating revenue of ₹37.6234 crore became ₹38.1113 crore in the subsequent comparative when duty drawback of ₹0.2507 crore and MEIS of ₹0.2372 crore moved from other income. FY21 annual revenue includes freight of ₹1.0367 crore that the IPO restated product-sales presentation excluded. A core-sales endpoint sensitivity still produces roughly 20.9% CAGR, so the score is not dependent on a tiny classification boundary. A reliable price/volume/FX decomposition is unavailable.

No material purchased business was identified in the reviewed statements. New subsidiary subscriptions and loans are not acquired revenue. Subsidiaries currently contribute little external revenue and incur losses, while consolidated reporting eliminates intra-group flows. Organic growth is therefore the best-supported explanation, without inventing a precise new-product contribution.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
paragraphs: The runway should be built from utilization and customer access, not a global dental TAM. In the 29 June 2026 call, management reported legacy utilization of 67–68%, theoretical legacy turnover around ₹125 crore at full capacity, and new-line utilization of 18–20%. These are management estimates, not engineering-certified schedules. Current sales cannot simply be divided by utilization because capacity definitions and product mix differ.

The model starts from TTM revenue of ₹75.1105 crore. Base growth of 12% is below the recent three-year CAGR; bear and bull assumptions are 3% and 20%. A transparent runway bridge assumes an opening mix of 85% legacy and 15% new products. This is an analyst allocation, not reported segment data. Base legacy growth of 10% produces roughly ₹103 crore in year five, below the stated legacy ceiling; new products must earn the residual. Every scenario funds incremental fixed assets and working capital rather than assuming spare factory capacity means costless growth.

Three-year incremental NOPAT of ₹3.4651 crore on incremental invested capital of ₹11.8820 crore gives 29.16%. The five-year result is 31.19%. Adding operating cash equal to 5% of sales lowers the returns to 26.71% and 29.44%. Both exceed the analyst capital-cost range of 12–16%. The three-year capital addition includes ₹9.6021 crore of operating working capital and ₹2.2799 crore of fixed assets, highlighting cash absorption outside the factory.

These are coherent same-business bridges, not private project cohorts. FY21 reserve and depreciation adjustments weaken long-window precision, and immature new lines may earn less than legacy assets. The base model uses 2.5 times incremental sales-to-fixed-capital, maintenance capex and depreciation of 2.7% of sales, and explicit working-capital days. Inventory and payable days throughout are SALES-denominator proxies, not standard COGS/purchases days. Longer collections, inventory build and lower asset turns are tested.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
paragraphs: The Modi family controls the business. At 31 March 2026, audited consolidated Note 2(e), printed page 152, reports Atul Modi holding 4,503,680 shares (37.52%) and Namrata Modi 4,324,920 shares (36.03%): 8,828,600 promoter shares, or 73.55% using the reported rounded percentages. This is a dated year-end ownership baseline, not verified cutoff free float or pledge status. The 2021 prospectus figure of 73.60% is retained only as history. Issued capital is independently verified from the dated master, while cutoff ownership changes and encumbrance remain unverified.

The FY26 secretarial audit identifies delayed director-event disclosures and executive remuneration exceeding approved limits. A waiver of recovery of ₹11.38 lakh paid to Sai Kalyan Surapaneni over FY25 and FY26 passed at the 17 September 2026 AGM with 8,839,400 votes in favour and 132,000 against, or 98.53%. The complete voting filing resolves the vote outcome, not the original control lapse. FY26 aggregate director remuneration of ₹4.5855 crore is 22.4% of group PAT and 31.0% of CFO, a legitimate stewardship concern but not proof of diversion.

The change from Mittal & Associates to A D V & Associates follows term expiry and shareholder approval, not an identified auditor resignation. CARO discloses subsidiary demand loans without stipulated repayment tenure but no overdue amount beyond 90 days. No bank debt/default, reported fraud or material statutory arrears was identified in the reviewed scope. Related-party loans and investments disappear in consolidation through ordinary eliminations, not unexplained cash disappearance.

Execution is mixed. The IPO plan anticipated commissioning by FY22, yet CWIP was ₹16.8872 crore in FY23 and transferred into productive assets by FY24. Disinfectants were described as commercialized in FY26. The June 2026 call reported digital-resin growth of 40%, but Oradox sales fell 2%, while an indigenous printer was targeted for 2028. These are milestones to verify, not future earnings already earned. The delivery table preserves both achieved scaling and delays.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
paragraphs: The history keeps standalone FY21–26 and consolidated FY24–26 separate. Operating EBIT equals PBT plus finance cost less all other income. Finance costs of ₹0.1871 crore in FY21 and ₹0.1042 crore in FY22 are added back. All treasury income is excluded before applying an operating earnings multiple; cash is valued separately. FY26 group operating EBIT of ₹22.6972 crore and depreciation/amortization of ₹2.0088 crore imply operating EBITDA of ₹24.7060 crore, below a headline measure that includes other income.

Cash realization is mixed but substantial. FY22–26 standalone CFO/PAT is 71.93%; FY24–26 group conversion is 75.30%. Deposit interest is classified in investing cash flow while included in profit. Removing after-tax interest from the PAT denominator at an assumed 25% tax rate raises conversion to 81.84% and 87.90%, respectively. This is not an add-back of uncollected debtors. FY26 group inventory of ₹10.8939 crore, receivables of ₹8.7117 crore and supplier advances of ₹2.0383 crore deserve monitoring. Receivables over six months are ₹0.0273 crore; reported good status does not guarantee collection.

The FY21 comparative prints CFO of ₹1.8955 crore, duplicating the tax line. Its own pre-working-capital amount of ₹9.4813 crore plus changes of ₹1.1705 crore less tax of ₹1.8955 crore produces ₹8.7563 crore, also reconciling the cash movement. IPO restated CFO of ₹8.6055 crore is a different basis and is not silently substituted. FY23 original CFO of ₹10.6671 crore became ₹10.4277 crore when a ₹0.2394 crore payable outflow was included in the later comparative. An opening cash/equity difference of ₹0.0171 crore remains unexplained but bounded. Reserve-routed earlier depreciation reversal of ₹0.8069 crore and gratuity of ₹0.1310 crore constrain long-window capital-return precision.

The main current disclosure question is mutual-fund NAV. FY26 carrying cost is ₹8.6904 crore but the printed market value is ₹5.6098 crore; its comparative prints ₹4.7004 crore cost and ₹2.4262 crore market value. Both market cells repeat the values printed for FY25/FY24 in AR25. That strongly suggests stale copied cells, not a demonstrated ₹3.0806 crore loss. The apparent difference is 15.0% of PAT and 2.47% of equity if treated as current, but current NAV is unverified. The lower-cost/fair-value policy requires a holdings and valuation reconciliation. All ₹8.6904 crore is excluded from base funding and value; optional asset values are sensitivities only.

The main audit and IFC opinions are unmodified. Axiodent and Gulf statements are management-certified and unaudited: combined external revenue of ₹0.1263 crore is 0.176% of group sales, while absolute negative net assets of ₹0.7517 crore are 0.60% of group equity. Indian audit trails were enabled with no tampering identified; the foreign systems are not independently covered. CARO and contingent-liability notes do not identify a material default, fraud, title defect or statutory arrear in the reviewed scope. This is not a blanket guarantee about undisclosed or future events.

Group cash reconciles as ₹60.8984 crore opening cash plus CFO of ₹14.8086 crore, investing cash flow of −₹1.5892 crore, financing cash flow of −₹1.2003 crore and FX of −₹0.0638 crore, reaching ₹72.8537 crore versus ₹72.8538 crore reported, a rounding difference. Deposits of ₹56.6272 crore mature in three to twelve months and are not all cash on demand. The December 2025 no-deviation statement does not quantify remaining IPO use. The model therefore withholds the full ₹22.9496 crore actual net IPO proceeds. This is a conservative assumption, not an asserted current restriction.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
paragraphs: The primary method values terminal operating EBIT plus retained accessible cash less the operating reserve, with dated dividends. ₹405 and 12,003,000 shares imply ₹486.1215 crore market capitalization. TTM reported P/E is about 22.38 times. The EV cross-check subtracts reported cash only after the full IPO holdback and ₹5 crore reserve. No mutual funds or operating property are added. Broad reported net cash of ₹72.8538 crore is not equated with distributable cash.

Base assumptions are 12% growth, 30% operating EBIT margin and a 15-times terminal EBIT multiple. Bear assumptions are 3%, 23% and 10 times; bull assumptions are 20%, 33% and 18 times. Quarterly ledgers begin on 31 March 2026 and pre-fund operating outflows, taxes, working-capital build, capex and dividends before receipts. Old tax, capital creditors and the pre-entry FY26 dividend are settled once. The model does not count a subsidiary subscription both as group cash loss and an independent investment asset.

An independent FCFF DCF uses 12/14/16% WACC and 3/4/5% terminal growth with continuing growth reinvestment. It adds entry surplus once, not terminal retained cash again. The share of value derived from the terminal period is disclosed. All horizon calculations use actual dated intervals and a 365.25-day denominator, with no post-terminal funding leakage.

Reverse expectations require a finite funded bracket crossing. At a 15-times exit and 30% margin, ₹405 requires roughly 20.1% revenue CAGR to earn 15%, against the 12% base case. At 18 times, the required CAGR is about 15.6%. A root without funded support is NS, not the last tested endpoint. Entry estimates at 12/15/18% hurdles and execution costs of 0/1/2% are preserved.

Stresses cover growth versus exit multiple, receivables versus capex, margins versus inventory, available cash versus reserve, and IPO holdback versus optional fund value. Availability discounts apply AFTER the IPO holdback to avoid excluding the same cash twice. A hypothetical ₹65 crore expansion shock is unfinanced without rescue, so ordinary and conditional returns/entries are null. The explicit rescue issues whole shares at ₹324 with 2% fees before uses, including dividends on new shares. Rescue entry estimates are NS because a changed purchase price would require solving issue pricing and funding jointly.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
paragraphs: The strongest countercase is that historical returns came from a profitable legacy niche, while future growth needs more marketing, regulatory work, inventory and distributor credit. US/UAE subsidiaries could add cost without gaining profitable branded demand. Private-label growth may leave brand value outside the company. Digital resins face capable competitors; Oradox has already declined, and domestic FY26 growth was around 9%, not explosive.

The bear case links 3% growth to 23% margin, 70-day receivables, 80 inventory sales-days and a 10-times exit. It remains funded yet loses about 8.7% annually from ₹405. Severe stress combines declining revenue, 18% margins, 90-day receivables, 100 inventory sales-days and an eight-times exit; modeled annual loss is about 17.6%. Balance-sheet survival is not the same as protecting the purchase price.

Thesis-break conditions include persistent core margins below 25% with rising working capital, material unprovided losses, a regulatory or product-quality failure, substantiated related-party diversion, or large capital deployment without cash returns. A temporary quarter miss or an approved pay waiver alone is not a thesis break. Corrected NAV and proof of IPO utilization could improve confidence without improving the operating moat.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
paragraphs: Neither a fivefold nor a tenfold gain is central to this thesis. The model tests what revenue growth would produce those terminal share prices under base margin and multiple assumptions, requiring a finite funded solution. A separate rescue branch includes new money and ownership dilution. No funded crossing means NS, rather than reporting an unfinanced growth endpoint.

Fivefold price appreciation over five years requires roughly 38% annual price growth and tenfold about 58.5%, far above recent operating growth. The stated ₹125 crore legacy capacity ceiling does not establish those outcomes. A credible case would need quantified new-product revenue, repeat demand, global distribution, additional capacity and margin proof. Cash alone does not create adoption.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
paragraphs: The monitoring table connects current baselines to measurable milestones, warning levels and thesis breaks. Priorities are a corrected investment-NAV schedule, quantitative IPO utilization and deposit access. Sales growth must be reconciled to operating profit and cash rather than total income alone.

Before implementation, refresh actual BSE lot/series/surveillance, verify a full 60-session tape including zero-trade sessions, inspect spread/depth and obtain current encumbrance evidence. The illustrative ₹500,000 position is not the user’s disclosed holding or risk budget. At ₹405, six 200-share lots cost ₹486,000 and seven lots ₹567,000, excluding fees and impact.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
paragraphs: The business has credible growth and capital efficiency, but moderate competitive protection and mixed stewardship. It does not meet the framework compounder test: BQS is below 8 and GOV/MOAT are below 7, even though GQS exceeds 7. A strong growth score cannot cancel governance or valuation constraints.

Formal investment classification is Insufficient evidence because L is NS. Even the diagnostic IAS upper bound with L set to 10 remains below 5.5, so missing liquidity cannot rescue the current base valuation. The action category is research/watchlist, not a new-purchase endorsement. The ₹307.00 conditional 15% entry estimate depends on the stated operating and funding assumptions and cleared implementation evidence.

Reconsider after a current NAV reconciliation, quantified IPO utilization, verified execution capacity, cash-generative new-product growth, or a price offering the hurdle under a conservative funded case. Main-board migration alone would not increase operating earnings value. This is not a personalized sell instruction for existing holders, whose taxes, weight and liquidity needs are unknown.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
paragraphs: The source chain prioritizes issuer annual reports, the SEBI IPO prospectus, audited FY26 results, limited-reviewed June 2026 results, the June earnings call, the September AGM vote and the December 2025 IPO no-deviation statement. Corporate filings on Business Standard are mirrored primary documents, not automated news conclusions. Source URLs, document dates, scope, locations and payload hashes are preserved in the register. Full source documents are not reproduced.

All historical financial amounts are in INR crore unless labelled otherwise. Operating working capital excludes cash, mutual funds, subsidiary funding, advance tax, accrued deposit interest and gratuity assets, while retaining genuine operating advances, receivables, inventory and liabilities. Invested capital includes PPE/intangibles, CWIP and operating working capital. Forecast tax of 25%, capital cost of 12–16%, growth, margins, working-capital days and reserves are analyst assumptions.

Open questions include current mutual-fund NAV and carrying-value reconciliation; remaining IPO earmarks; deposit break terms; customer/distributor concentration and retention; price-volume mix; new-product unit economics; promoter encumbrance/free float; and full cutoff surveillance and 60-session turnover. Reproduction verifies arithmetic and consistency, not missing source authentication or future outcomes.

name: Prevest Denpro Limited
summary:
Prevest Denpro is a profitable dental-materials manufacturer with recurring consumables, international distribution and substantial cash. The strongest evidence is a multi-year organic incremental-capital return near 30%, supported by actual operating cash generation. The concerns are a contestable moat, uneven new-product execution, governance and disclosure lapses, and a price that asks more than the conservative operating case delivers.

At the dated secondary historical reference close of ₹405 on 19 October 2026, the base case earns 8.77% nominal pretax annually over 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, below the 15% equity hurdle. The conditional 15% entry estimate is ₹307.00, not an executable bid or recommendation. Full investment attractiveness remains NS because the complete 60-session liquidity and restrictions evidence is unavailable. This is a research/watchlist candidate, not a certified compounder or a distressed financing situation.
